title: Adaptation Cost for Pointwise CATE Estimation under a Sharp Risk Budget
banked_reason: The proposed sharp, sequence-independent minimax constant is replaced by an unmatched positive liminf/limsup bracket; equality with the covariance game and the sharp dual attainer remain OEQs, so the current theorem is a weaker exponential-order result rather than the promised headline contribution.
gap_reasons: The proposed sharp, sequence-independent minimax constant is replaced by an unmatched positive liminf/limsup bracket; equality with the covariance game and the sharp dual attainer remain OEQs, so the current theorem is a weaker exponential-order result rather than the promised headline contribution.

The delivered result establishes an exponential-order adaptation bracket and an observable selector satisfying the exact rough-risk budget; it does not establish the requested sequence-independent sharp constant or its attainer.
Fixed-code information spectra leave full-class composite testing unresolved, while the covariance programs establish neither gap convergence nor equality with the statistical frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: Attempted a sequence-independent sharp minimax adaptation coefficient, certified covariance-game approximations, and a matching exact-budget estimator. Supervisor-approved two-pass recovery preserved all twelve support proofs and proved honest bracket/order headlines; all four external citations were directly attested. The two load-bearing OEQs (finite-approximation completeness and covariance-saddle equivalence) remain open, so the promised sharp kernel was not delivered; no Lean formalization was launched.
tldr: The proved contribution is a two-sided exponential adaptation bracket for the pointwise observational CATE under the exact rough-risk allowance \(Bn^{-1/4}\), with nuisance Hölder orders \(1/10\) and \(1\) and a Lipschitz effect in both unchanged classes. For every \(B_n\to\infty\) with \(B_n^8=o(\log n)\), the normalized negative logarithm of the constrained frontier has positive liminf and limsup bounded above by \((147\sqrt2/20)\{1+2(1-\log2)^2\}<13\). One explicit clipped local-arm-average and disjoint-pair selector has rough risk at most \(3B_nr_n/4\) and smooth risk at most \(r_n\exp(-c_{\exp}B_n^8)\) eventually. The inherited internal exponential envelope and selector receive credit as the achievability architecture. Legal four-cell cancellation and fixed finite-profile information spectra provide the same-experiment converse. Finite rational field codes and an outer moment program give certified one-sided brackets for the separate covariance infimum; any returned midpoint has a certified error, but the tolerance scan may continue indefinitely. Sharp-limit existence, equality with the covariance game, gap convergence, and a finite-dual sharp attainer remain the two explicit open questions. These results are a scalar uniform-design benchmark for the same CATE estimand studied by Wendling et al. (2018), with prospective methodological use rather than a direct reanalysis.
gap: Tsybakov (1998) already obtains exact pointwise and sup-norm adaptation in Gaussian white noise on Sobolev classes, and Butucea (2001) gives an explicit exact adaptive density constant. These close noncausal antecedents and Kennedy et al.\textquotesingle s fixed-smoothness CATE rates do not determine the exact finite-sample frontier \(A_n(B)\) in the observational binary-treatment experiment. The missing result combines four-cell legality and cancellation, the period-bearing covariance-profile game, and a causal data-only attainer satisfying the exact rough-risk allowance.
fill: The result spine derives legal same-experiment paths, proves the randomized-treatment reduction, and resolves full-class covariance equivalence and finite inner-outer approximation before using the dual to construct an exact-budget estimator. Its certified lower and upper brackets for \(I_{\mathrm{var}}\), combined with the dual construction, calibrate the finite profile grid, rejection threshold, and deterministic budget reserve of the Kennedy et al.-style higher-order local \(R\)-learner and dual-test selector, deciding whether a claimed adaptation guarantee meets the exact rough-risk constraint. The brackets and induced selector calibration give a reproducible scalar uniform-\(X\) benchmark for developing and stress testing methods for the same observational binary-treatment, binary-outcome CATE estimand studied by Wendling et al. (2018), rather than a direct reanalysis of their data.
